findings.reason: without `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` the call that writes the pending record before promotion cannot be moved or cleared, so the node as written cannot satisfy its own done-when.
findings.text: §12 requires that a refused `crew complete --land` leave "no promotion commit, no release commit, no ledger row and no pending-landing record", but the ordering that produces those writes is in `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`: `pending_landing.write_pending` runs before `crew_module.complete` (:3601 before :3605), the land runs after promotion (:3652), `clear_pending` is reached only on a successful land (`_land_a_promoted_run`, :3933), and a post-promotion failure is caught and turned into a refusal (:3923). The shortfall the section cites is computed in `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:808`, not in `promotion.py:728` as the Why states (that line only unpacks the returned value). Neither `crew_run_commands.py` nor `promotion_evidence.py` is in the section's write paths, so a worker fenced to `promotion.py`, `pending_landing.py`, `recovery_repair_dispatch.py` and the new test cannot deliver the stated endpoint and will either report a scope blocker or leave the defect standing

findings.reason: splitting the stale-record cleanup into its own section, or dropping it, changes what a node is scored on.
findings.text: §12's deliverable joins two endpoints that fail independently and are repaired in different modules: "either lands the head it cites, or refuses before writing anything" (promotion's commit-list presentation plus the pending-landing write ordering, `promotion.py` / `pending_landing.py`), and "a pending-landing record whose run's cited head is already merged is cleared by the next merge-repair pass and never resurrects the run" (the repair pass, `recovery_repair_dispatch.py`). The done-when's two cases exercise one each, so a single verdict would close a section whose record-cleanup half could be broken and unreported, and the gate proves neither property alone

findings.reason: a wrong root cause sends the repair at the shortfall report, which is deliberately non-fatal, while the refusal-after-writes ordering the section exists to fix is left unchanged.
findings.text: the Why states the call "refused with `commit_list_shortfall`", but `_require_gate_evidence` (`reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:808`) returns the shortfall as a value and its docstring is explicit that a shortfall "must not turn a passing promotion into a failed one" (:853); promotion stores it on the result (:882) and records it on the row (:1871). Nothing raises it, so it cannot have been the refusal. The run's own landing record for r-20261113T012546102955 shows the refusal at `stage_retry` with "Unable to create '/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.git/index.lock': File exists", after the two commit steps had already succeeded. The section's real defect — a post-promotion failure is converted to a refusal while the promotion, its release commit, its ledger row and the pending record stand — is genuine and reproducible from that record, but the named cause points a worker at the shortfall path instead of at the write ordering

findings.reason: a repair brief is required to confirm the defect reproduces before repair, and a worker told to clear a record that is not there cannot confirm it, while the head 23c73bb6b8 the plan quotes is still unintegrated in the run's worktree (release.json) — which is the fact worth citing instead.
findings.text: §12 states "The pending-landing record still points at 23c73, and discarding it risks the resurrection path", but `~/.config/reckon/crew/pending-landings/` holds fifteen records and none names run r-20261113T012546102955, head 23c73bb6b8 or its project; a search of that directory for the head returns nothing. The reason is structural: `pending_landing.write_pending` (`reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:64`) writes only run_id, project, written_at, attempts and the pointer — it records no head and no status at all, and the `awaiting-review` status the plan quotes is written by the admit service's lander (`reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:391`), a different writer. So the named artifact cannot be the one the plan describes, and the live risk the section cites as motivation no longer exists

findings.reason: an open driving followup for a section declared done re-dispatches finished work, and the plan's own state-integrity rule requires the driving followup to be resolved when a section lands.
